topics.label: Rocks
facts: Rocks are made of minerals, which are natural materials found in Earth.
Igneous rocks form when hot melted rock cools and hardens.
Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sand, mud, and small stones pressed together over a long time.
Metamorphic rocks form when other rocks are squeezed and heated deep inside Earth.

questions.fact: Rocks are made of minerals, natural materials found in the Earth.

choices: Hot melted rock cools and hardens
questions.fact: When melted rock called magma cools, it hardens into igneous rock.

questions.q: Which rock forms from layers pressed together over a long time?
questions.fact: Sedimentary rocks form when layers of sand and mud are pressed together.

questions.q: What can change one rock into a metamorphic rock?
choices: Heat and pressure deep inside Earth
questions.fact: Deep inside Earth, heat and squeezing pressure change rocks into metamorphic rocks.

topics.label: Volcanoes
facts: A volcano is a mountain that can erupt with hot melted rock called lava.
The melted rock inside Earth is called magma, and it is called lava once it flows out.
Volcanoes form where Earth's plates move apart or push together.
When a volcano erupts, it can send out lava, ash, and gases.

questions.q: What is the hot melted rock that flows out of a volcano called?
questions.fact: Melted rock is called magma inside Earth and lava once it flows out.

choices: A mountain that can erupt with lava
questions.fact: A volcano is an opening in Earth's crust where lava, ash, and gases can escape.

questions.q: What do we call melted rock while it is still inside Earth?
questions.fact: Magma is melted rock below the surface; it becomes lava when it erupts.

questions.q: What else can a volcano send out besides lava?
questions.fact: Eruptions can throw out ash clouds and hot gases as well as lava.

topics.label: Earthquakes
facts: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground.
Earthquakes happen when rocks deep inside Earth suddenly move along a crack called a fault.
Scientists measure earthquakes with a tool called a seismograph.
The strength of an earthquake is often given as a number on a scale.

choices: A sudden shaking of the ground
questions.fact: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground caused by rocks moving deep inside Earth.

questions.q: What is the crack in Earth's crust where rocks move called?
questions.fact: Faults are cracks in Earth's crust where rocks can suddenly slip.

questions.q: What tool do scientists use to measure earthquakes?
questions.fact: A seismograph records the shaking of the ground during an earthquake.

questions.q: What should you do during an earthquake indoors?
questions.fact: Drop under a strong table, cover your head, and hold on until the shaking stops.

topics.label: Soil
facts: Soil is made of tiny pieces of rock, dead plants and animals, water, and air.
It can take hundreds of years for just a few centimetres of soil to form.
Earthworms help soil by tunnelling through it and breaking dead leaves into rich earth.
Plants need soil to hold them up and to give them water and nutrients to grow.

choices: Tiny rock pieces, dead plants, water, and air
questions.fact: Soil is a mix of broken rock, decayed plants and animals, water, and air.

questions.q: How long can it take for a few centimetres of soil to form?
questions.fact: Soil forms very slowly, over hundreds of years.

questions.q: Which animal helps make soil healthy?
questions.fact: Earthworms tunnel through soil and turn dead leaves into rich earth.

choices: Water and nutrients, and something to hold onto
questions.fact: Soil holds plants in place and supplies them with water and nutrients.
